# bin2cpp

Embeds binary files into a C++ source file as one package, so a program can read them without opening any file.

```
bin2cpp -p <package> -o <output folder> [-n <namespace>] [-r <root>] [--align <n>] <file>... [@<response file>]...
```

It writes `<output folder>/<package>.h` and `<package>.cpp`. The `.cpp` holds every file in one `uint8_t` array, in
the order given, each file's bytes behind a comment with its path. The header declares a span over the whole package
and one per file, in the namespace:

```cpp
// Generated by bin2cpp, do not edit.
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

namespace game::assets {

extern const std::span<const std::uint8_t> kPackage;

// materials/toon.mat
extern const std::span<const std::uint8_t> kMaterialsToon;

}
```

The spans are `constinit`, so they can be read during the static initialization of other translation units.

| Option              | Meaning |
|---------------------|---------|
| `-p`, `--package`   | Name of the generated files. Must be a C++ identifier. |
| `-o`                | Output folder, created if missing. |
| `-n`, `--namespace` | Optional. The namespace of the spans, e.g. `game::assets`. Default: the package name. |
| `-r`, `--root`      | Optional. Symbols are made from each file's path relative to this folder, and every file must be inside it. Without it, from the file name. |
| `--align`           | Each file starts at a multiple of this many bytes (a power of two, default 16), so SPIR-V and other word-sized data can be read in place. The array is aligned to it and padded with zeros between files. `--align 1` packs them tightly. |
| `@<file>`           | Reads more files from a response file, one path per line. |

A file's symbol is made from its path (relative to the root, or just the file name) without the last extension: the
letters and digits are split into words at every other character, and each word is capitalized behind a `k`.
`tonemap.vert.spv` is `kTonemapVert`, and `materials/toon.mat` is `kToon`, or `kMaterialsToon` when the root is the
folder holding `materials/`. Two files with the same symbol, or a file named `kPackage`, are an error.

The outputs are only rewritten when their content changes, so a build that restats them recompiles nothing when the
files are unchanged. The source is about six times the size of the files.
